item.title: Clean-Life Living — Sat Oct 24, 3:30 PM — Union Congregational Church
item.description: From Hip-Hop to Holistic Health: Clean-Life LIVING Brings Fresh Perspectives on Living Well to Montclair Darryl “DMC” McDaniels, Dr. Brian Clement, Warren Zanes and other notable guests come together October 24 for an afternoon of inspiration, connection and community benefiting Montclair Helps. MONTCLAIR, NJ — What do a hip-hop legend, a holistic wellness pioneer, a rock musician and bestselling author, a community builder and a scholar of American transcendentalism have in common? More than you might think. On Saturday, October 24, Montclair will host Clean-Life LIVING, an afternoon designed to explore what it means to live well in an increasingly complicated, demanding and often disconnected world. Taking place from 3:30 to 6:30 p.m. at Union Congregational Church, the event brings together an eclectic group of speakers whose experiences span music, nutrition, psychology, creativity, philosophy and community building. item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Sat Oct 24, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.description:

After 12 years of bucolic bliss, Mr. Fox breaks a promise to his wife and raids the farms of their human neighbors, Boggis, Bunce, and Bean. Giving in to his animal instincts endangers not only his marriage but also the lives of his family and their animal friends. item.title: Writing: Method & Motivation — Wed Nov 4, 6:15 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
A workshop for anyone who wants to write or wants to infuse their existing writing practice with new energy. In each class, we'll consider one element of fiction or creative non-fiction, such as point of view, narrative voice, and what makes a piece of writing riveting, or boring. Students can expect in-class writing prompts, reading aloud, and optional homework. Positive encouragement, rather than formal critiques, will be featured, and inspiration and organization for writers will be discussed. Students should bring whatever they use to write to each class.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:

This writing group will run over 13 weeks during the Spring semester (January - April 2027), with a week off in March. item.title: Life Long Learning: The History of American Anti-Semitic Terrorism & Current Threats with Stuart Wexler — Wed Dec 16, 1:00 PM — JCC MetroWest | Tepper Hall
item.description:
Given the current climate of anti-Semitism in our country, Stuart Wexler will discuss the history of anti-Semitic violence in the United States and its relevance to today’s situation. His work explores how anti-Semitic violence and racial terrorism are often driven by the same overlooked ideologies, a connection that is as relevant today as it was 60 years ago. About the speaker: Stuart Wexler is a historian and a teacher, who specializes in the history of American domestic terrorism. He is the author of 4 books including America’s Secret Jihad: The Hidden History of Religious Terrorism in the United States. FREE for JCC Member; $15 Nonmember
Register Here
Grandchildren home on college break are welcome to attend for free.
Source: JCC MetroWest
